 Judgment

On 11.08.2020 Pavan Kumar asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the insurer and owner of Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA- 05-AH-9459 alleging that on 11.06.2020 at 1.25 p.m. when riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HG-1849 from Magadi towards Kunigal, near Kalari cross, Magadi Taluk, driver of Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-05-AH-9459 drove the same negligently from the opposite direction on the wrong part of the road, dashed the same to motorcycle , thereby caused accident, caused injuries to petitioner Pavan Kumar.

2. Immediately after the accident Pavan Kumar has been admitted to Government Hospital, Magadi wherein first aid has been provided, then admitted to KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru wherein took treatment as inpatient from 11.06.2020 to 20.06.2020.
3. As on the date of accident Pavan Kumar being aged 21 years, used to earn Rs.25,000/-p.m. by working as Electrician.
4. Regarding in the accident Magadi police registered crime No.115/2020.
5. In response to the notice, respondent No.1 owner of the Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-05-AH-9459 appeared through his Advocate but neither filed written statement nor participated in the proceedings.

6. In response to the notice, the respondent No.2- insurance company appeared through his Advocate and on 26.03.2022 filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

7. On the basis of the pleadings on 25.10.2022, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 11.06.2020 at about 1.25 p.m. on Magadi Kunigal Road, near Kalari cross in Kasaba Hobli, Magadi Taluk of Ramanagara, he being the rider of the Pulsar Motor Cycle bearing Reg.
Pavan Kumar .C.J vs Kokila Enterprises on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196470325/
2 No.KA-06/HG-1849 had met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of the Tipper Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AH-9459 by its driver and he sustained injuries in the accident as averred?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation and if so, what amount and from whom?
3. What Order ?

8. On 15.06.2022 Pavan Kumar deposed as PW1 and produced 12 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.12.
9.
On 20.12.2022 Pavan Kumar expired.
On 14.03.2023 the legal representatives of Pavan Kumar filed IA No.III seeking permission to get implead as legal heirs of Pavan Kumar and continue the litigation.

After hearing the submission made on behalf of both the parties through a speaking order dated 26.05.2023 this authority allowed IA No.III, thereby permitted legal heirs of Pavan Kumar to get implead as petitioners in the petition.
10. On 08.06.2023 the learned advocate appearing for the petitioners reported amendment of petition i.e., inserting the names of the L.Rs of Pavan Kumar in the petition.

11. In view of the death of Pavan Kumar and impleading of legal heirs of Pavan Kumar as petitioners on 26.07.2024 this authority framed the following additional issue:
Whether present petitioners proves that due to the injuries suffered in the accident dated 11.06.2020 on 20.12.2022 Pavan Kumar C.J., (original petitioner) expired?
12.

On 26.07.2024, 6.11.2024 petitioner No.1(a) -
Jayashankar deposed as PW.2 and produced 4 documents at Ex.P.13 to P.16.
13.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of petitioner and perused the records.

14. On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 ... Compensation is assessed at  Rs.18,64,442/- with interest at  6% p.a. from 20.12.2022.
Additional Issue ...
In the Negative  Issue No.3 ...

Issue No.1 :- In the lengthy argument learned advocate appearing for the petitioners by analyzing the evidence available in the file requested to answer issue No.1 in favour of petitioners by relying on the following judgments:
1. 2010 ACJ 736 dated 23.04.2008 - Karan Singh V/s Anshuman and others 2. 2011 AIR SCW 1530 dated 18.02.2011-Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others 16.

entities.text: Karan Singh V/s Anshuman and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of the judgments cited above with reference to the submission made on behalf of both the parties, I have appreciated the material available in the file.

17. In evidence affidavit PW1 Pavan Kumar stated that on 11.06.2020 at 1.25 p.m.
when he was riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HG-1849 from Magadi towards Kunigal, near Kalari cross, Magadi Taluk, driver of Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-05-AH-9459 drove the same negligently from the opposite direction on the wrong part of the road, dashed the same to motorcycle , thereby caused accident,
caused injuries to petitioner Pavan Kumar.
18.

PW.1 further stated that immediately after the accident he was shifted to Government Hospital, Magadi wherein first aid treatment has been provided, then admitted to KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru wherein took treatment as inpatient from 11.06.2020 to 20.06.2020 and underwent surgery.
19. In the written statement, respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegation regarding reason, mode of the accident.
20. In this case during lifetime of PW.1 - Pavan Kumar, respondent No.2-insurance company has not cross-examined Pavan Kumar.

21. Ex.P.1 is the copy of FIR pertaining to crime No.115/2020 registered by Magadi police on 19.06.2020 against the driver of Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-05-AH- 9459 for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPC and under Sec.187 of MV Act regarding the accident taken place on 11.06.2020 at 1.25 p.m. on Magadi - Kunigal road,
near Kilari cross, between two wheeler bearing No.KA-06-HG-1849 and Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-05-AH-9459 resulting in the injuries to petitioner Pavan Kumar on the basis of complaint of presented by PW.2- Jayashankar S/o Tandavachar.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of the complaint dated 19.06.2020.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of the spot mahazar dated 19.06.2020.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of the Tipper lorry seizure mahazar dated 24.06.2020.

Ex.P.5 is the copy of the chargesheet dated 22.09.2020 filed by Magadi police in crime No.115/2020 against Kisan Rathod @ Kissan Somalu Chowhan S/o. Somulu -driver of Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-05-AH-9459 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of IPC Section 187 of IMV Act.
Ex.P.6 is the motor vehicle accident report dated 24.06.2020.

Ex.P.7 is the copy of the wound certificate issued Pavan Kumar .C.J vs Kokila Enterprises on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196470325/
4 by KIMS hospital, Bengaluru in which reason for the injuries suffered by Pavan Kumar is noted as RTA.

Ex.P.8 is the Discharge Summary issued by KIMS hospital, Bengaluru in which reason for the injuries noted as RTA two wheeler vs Tipper lorry at around 2 pm 11.06.2020 near Kalari gate,
Magadi.

entities.text: RTA two wheeler vs Tipper lorry
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 22. In this case respondent No.1 and 2 have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by Pavan Kumar regarding reason and mode of the accident and nature of injuries suffered by Pavan Kumar in the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on on 11.06.2020 at 1.25 p.m. when Pavan Kumar was riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HG-1849 from Magadi towards Kunigal, near Kalari cross, Magadi Taluk, Kisan Rathod @ Kissan Somalu Chowhan S/o.

Somulu -driver of Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-05-AH-9459 drove the same negligently from the opposite direction on the wrong part of the road, dashed the same to motorcycle, thereby caused accident,
caused injuries to petitioner Pavan Kumar.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
23. Additional Issue:
In the evidence PW.2- Jayashankar stated that in the accident Pavan Kumar suffered grievous injuries, took first aid at Government Hospital, Magadi, then took treatment at KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru.

PW.2 submitted that in the accident Pavan Kumar suffered fracture of shaft of right femur middle 1/3rd, fracture distal end of radius with ulnar styloid fracture, fracture of 4th metacarpal right hand, severe injuries to legs, head.
PW.2 stated that his son underwent surgery on 12.06.2020 and spent Rs.3,00,000/- for treatment.
24. In para No.5 of the affidavit PW.2 stated that due to the accidental injuries on 20.12.2022 Pavan Kumar expired.

25. In the cross-examination PW.2 denied the suggestion that fractures of Pavan Kumar are not treated by inserting rod and only one day Pavan kumar has been treated at KIMS Hospital,
Bengaluru.
PW.2 submitted readiness to produce the evidence of doctor who treated Pavan Kumar.
PW.2 admitted that after 2 years 2 months from the date of the accident Pavan Kumar expired.

26. Wound certificate, discharge summary, medical bills shows that in the incident Pavan Kumar suffered lacerated wound over right thigh, right forearm, base of little finger and ring finger,
abrasion over right thigh and knee, tenderness over right thigh, hand and knee, displaced fracture of mid shaft femur, fracture of ulnar styloid process, fracture of radial styloid process, comminuted fracture of base of 4th and 5th metacarpal bone, chip fracture of tip of right fibula, took treatment at KIMS hospital, Bengaluru from 11.06.2020 to 26.06.2020 by spending Rs.1,68,442/-.
27.
In the file there are no evidence to show that treatment if any taken by Pavan Kumar subsequent to 26.06.2020 date of discharge for the injuries suffered in the accident.
As referred above on 15.06.2022 i.e., after 2 years from the date of accident Pavan Kumar deposed before this authority i.e., date of evidence affidavit.

28. In the file there are no evidence to show that in view of injuries suffered in the accident dated 11.06.2020 in spite of treatment taken at KIMS hospital, Bengaluru on 20.12.2022 Pavan Kumar expired.

The evidence available in the file are insufficient to infer that on 20.12.2022 Pavan Kumar Pavan Kumar .C.J vs Kokila Enterprises on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196470325/
5 expired due to nature and consequences of the injuries suffered in the accident dated 11.06.2020.

sentences.text: Hence, I came to the conclusion that petitioners are failed to prove the allegations that due to the injuries suffered in the accident dated 11.06.2020 at 1.25 p.m. Pavan Kumar expired on 22.12.2022.
Hence, I answer Additional Issue in the Negative.
29. Issue No.2:
In the petition/evidence affidavit Pavan Kumar stated that as on the date of accident being aged about 21 years, use to earn Rs.25,000/- per month by working as Electrician.
30. In the written statement respondent No.2 insurance company denied the age, occupation and income of Pavan Kumar.
31. In the evidence affidavit PW.2 Jayashankar stated that prior to the accident Pavan Kumar use to earn Rs.25,000/- by working as Electrician.
32. In the cross-examination PW.2 submitted inability to produce documents regarding income of Pavan Kumar.
33. In Ex.P.12 copy of the aadhaar card of Pavan Kumar the date of birth is noted as 01.06.1999.
As referred above the medical bills shows that since 11.06.2020 to 20.06.2020 Pavan Kumar took treatment by spending Rs.1,68,442/-.
The materials available in the file shows that during pendency of the petition on 20.12.2022 Pavan Kumar expired.

34. Hence, I have calculated loss of dependency in the following terms:
Age of Pavan Kumar as on the date of 21 years accident - Notional monthly income of Pavan Kumar Rs.14,500/- Less: 50% towards personal expenses Rs.7,250/- (14,500-7,250(50%)= 7,250)

Loss of future income 7250x12x18 Rs.15,66,000/-
35.

Hence, I assess compensation under the head of loss of dependency at Rs.15,66,000/-, under the head of loss to estate at Rs.15,000/-, under the head of funeral expenses at Rs.15,000/-, under the head of loss of consortium at Rs.80,000/- (40,000x2), under the head of treatment charges at Rs.1,68,442/-, under the head of attendants, conveyance and nourishment charges at Rs.20,000/-.
Sl
. No .
Head of Compensation Amount/
Rs 1. Loss of dependency 15,66,000-00 2. Loss of estate 15,000-00 3.
Funeral expenses 15,0000-00 4.
Loss of Consortium to 80,000-00 Rs.40,000/each Pavan Kumar .C.J vs Kokila Enterprises on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196470325/
6 5. Towards Treatment charges 1,68,442-00 6. Attendants, conveyance and 20,000-00 nourishment charges
Hence, I assess total compensation at Rs.18,64,442/- with interest at 6% p.a.. from 20.12.2022 (date of death of Pavan Kumar).
Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly.
37. Issue No.4:
In the written statement respondent No.2 admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-05-AH-9459 as on the date of incident.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of incident , respondent No.1 owner of Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-05-AH-9459 has violated any terms of the policy.

38. However. in view of finding on record regarding Additional Issue, in this case present petitioners (legal representatives of Pavan Kumar) are not entitle to receive compensation from the respondents.

Hence, I answer issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER

The petition dated 11.08.2020 filed by Pavan Kumar who expired on 20.12.2022 and then continued by his legal representatives under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation from the respondents, who are the insurer and owner of Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-05-AH-9459 is hereby dismissed.
There is no order as to costs.

(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 10th day of February , 2025)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
